column1: A ball begins to swing as a simple pendulum from its maximum amplitude. A cube is suspended on the pendulum line and swings left and right under the influence of gravity. A point mass gradually decreases its swing amplitude under the effect of air resistance. A ball is released at a position forming a 45-degree angle with the pendulum line and begins to swing. A simple pendulum is analyzed and compared under different pendulum lengths. Two balls as a double pendulum system influence each other and produce complex motion. A ball passes through a magnetic field region during its swing and is acted upon by force. A ball swings as a simple pendulum in a vacuum environment to observe motion without air resistance. A ball acts as a simple pendulum in water to observe the effect of water resistance on motion. A ball is driven by periodic external forces during its swing, resulting in resonance. A ball as a simple pendulum is slightly pushed away from its equilibrium position to start small amplitude oscillations. A ball is connected to a spring during its swing, observing the energy conversion between them. A ball is affected by a rotating platform during its swing, causing a change in its path. A simple pendulum's periodic changes under different amplitudes. A ball as a simple pendulum above an inclined plane to observe the changes in swing direction. A ball as a simple pendulum is released from rest and its initial speed is measured. A ball gradually stops due to friction during its swing. A ball is experimented as a simple pendulum under different gravitational environments. A ball's motion trajectory analysis as a simple pendulum under different initial angles. A ball performs vibration comparison experiments on pendulum lines with different line densities.
